Patient: I'm 86 years old, and I'm a male. I'm here because I've been having pain in my left arm, especially at night, and it's been going on for about two weeks. It started suddenly one morning and has been bothering me on and off since.
Doctor: Can you describe the nature of the arm pain (e.g., sharp, dull, throbbing)? Does it radiate to other areas? Have you experienced any associated symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, numbness, or tingling? Additionally, have you had any prior history of similar episodes or any known medical conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, or coronary artery disease?
Patient: The pain is more of a dull ache, but it can feel sharp at times, especially when I move my hand. It starts in my hand and goes all the way down my arm. I haven't had any chest pain or shortness of breath, but I do have some numbness and tingling in my hand. I also have neuropathy in this finger from an old injury, and I'm one percent disabled from leg issues. I don't have diabetes or heart problems, as far as I know.
Doctor: Have you undergone any prior cardiac evaluations, such as an electrocardiogram (ECG), echocardiogram, or stress test? If so, please provide the results or dates of these tests.
Patient: I don't recall having any heart tests done, to be honest. I've been focused on the arm pain and the issues with my leg, which is why I was referred here. I don't think I've had an ECG or anything like that before.
Doctor: Have you undergone any recent imaging studies, such as an X-ray, MRI, or CT scan of the arm, neck, or chest? If so, please provide the results or details of those examinations.
Patient: I don't recall having any recent imaging done on my arm or neck, but I was told I have arthritis in my neck from an X-ray. I haven't had an MRI yet, though.
Doctor: Have you experienced any recent trauma or injury to your neck or arm that could be related to the current symptoms?
Patient: No, I don't recall any recent trauma or injury to my neck or arm. The pain started suddenly one morning, and I don't remember anything happening to cause it. It just began hurting really bad, and I had to ice it to get some relief.
Doctor: Could you please describe the exact location of the pain in your left arm and hand, and whether it is accompanied by any weakness or changes in sensation, such as numbness or tingling, in specific areas?
Patient: The pain starts in my hand and goes all the way down my arm. I have some numbness and tingling in my hand, and I notice weakness when I try to grip things. My finger, which I hurt a while back, doesn't work properly either.
Doctor: Could you please provide details about any neurological deficits you are experiencing, such as weakness, numbness, or tingling in other parts of your body, and whether you have any history of cardiac issues or risk factors like hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or smoking?
Patient: I don't have any weakness, numbness, or tingling in other parts of my body besides my hand and that one finger. As far as I know, I don't have any heart issues or risk factors like high blood pressure or high cholesterol. I don't smoke, either.
Doctor: Could you please describe the current physical examination findings, including your vital signs and any neurological assessment of your upper extremity that has been performed?
Patient: I don't have the details of a physical exam done by another doctor, but when Dr. Miller examined me, he had me do some movements with my arms and checked my reflexes. He said my reflexes were all negative, and he didn't find any tenderness in my neck. He also had me squeeze his fingers to check my strength, and it felt about the same in both hands.
Doctor: Could you provide the results of the nerve conduction studies, imaging (such as MRI of the cervical spine), and ECG that are pending?
Patient: I don't have the results of any nerve conduction studies, MRI of my cervical spine, or ECG yet. Those tests are still pending, and I'm waiting to see what they show.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of the pending ECG, nerve conduction studies, and MRI of the cervical spine?
Patient: I don't have the results of any nerve conduction studies, MRI of my cervical spine, or ECG yet. Those tests are still pending, and I'm waiting to see what they show.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of the pending ECG, nerve conduction studies, and MRI of the cervical spine?
Patient: I don't have the results of any nerve conduction studies, MRI of my cervical spine, or ECG yet. Those tests are still pending, and I'm waiting to see what they show.
Doctor: Thank you for letting me know the tests are still pending. Once you receive the results of your ECG, nerve conduction studies, and MRI of the cervical spine, please share them with me so we can review them together and determine the next steps in your care.
Patient: I don't have the results of any nerve conduction studies, MRI of my cervical spine, or ECG yet. Those tests are still pending, and I'm waiting to see what they show.
Doctor: Thank you for letting me know the test results are still pending. I understand this can be concerning while waiting for the results. Once we have the ECG, nerve conduction studies, and MRI of the cervical spine, we will be able to better understand the cause of your symptoms. In the meantime, is there anything else you would like to share about your symptoms or concerns?
Patient: In the meantime, I don't have anything else to share about my symptoms. The pain in my left arm still comes and goes, especially at night, and I've noticed some weakness in my hand when gripping things. I'm just hoping the tests will help us figure out what's going on and how to make it better.
Doctor: Thank you for sharing that with me. I understand that the pain and weakness can be concerning. To better understand your condition, could you let me know if you've experienced any similar symptoms in the past or if there are any other factors that might be contributing to your discomfort?
Patient: I don't recall having any similar symptoms in the past, but I did hurt this finger some time ago, and it doesn't work properly or very rarely. Other than that, I don't know of any other factors contributing to the discomfort.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of the pending ECG, nerve conduction studies, and MRI of the cervical spine once they are available?

reference_so.subjective:
Basic information: 86-year-old male presenting with left arm pain for approximately two weeks, onset was sudden, and it has been intermittent, particularly at night.

History of present illness: Sudden onset of left arm pain approximately two weeks ago, which has been intermittent and particularly bothersome at night. The pain is more of a dull ache but can feel sharp at times, especially when moving the hand. It starts in the hand and radiates down the arm. There is associated numbness and tingling in the hand. The patient reports no recent trauma or injury to the neck or arm. The pain started suddenly one morning, and he does not remember anything happening to cause it. The patient also reports weakness when gripping things and impaired function in a finger from an old injury.

Past history: Neuropathy in this finger from an old injury; 1% disabled from leg issues; no known diabetes or heart problems.
reference_so.objective:
Physical examination: Physical examination by Dr. Miller included assessment of arm movements and reflexes. Reflexes were all negative, no tenderness in the neck was found, and strength testing showed equal grip strength in both hands.

Investigations: Auxiliary examination results are pending. Cardiac and neurological investigations, including ECG, nerve conduction studies, and MRI of the cervical spine, are still pending. The patient has a history of arthritis in the neck from an X-ray but has not had an MRI yet.
